questions.q: How many distinct symptoms does Elena Marsh describe in her January 31 call?
options: Three
Four
Six
Ten
questions.explain: Elena names six symptoms, spanning AP, AR, Assets, Cash Management, Subledger Accounting, and General Ledger.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does 'the books don't balance' usually mean in a real case like this one?
options: Debits literally no longer equal credits in posted journals
Subledgers don't reconcile to the GL, reports don't tie, and known items are sitting open — not a literal debit/credit break
The chart of accounts has been deleted
The fiscal calendar has the wrong number of periods
questions.explain: Double-entry accounting doesn't silently break; the phrase really describes reconciliation and reporting gaps, not a literal imbalance in posted journals.

questions.q: Which symptom does Elena describe that maps to the unposted intercompany journal from lesson 17?
options: Depreciation on new equipment looks heavier than expected
AP aging doesn't match the GL
Intercompany numbers between the US and Canada don't tie
A bank reconciliation item still isn't cleared
questions.explain: Elena's sixth symptom, intercompany not tying between the US and Canadian entities, maps directly to the unposted $27,750.00 journal planted in lesson 17.

questions.q: Which lesson is assigned to investigate the bank variance, the SLA gap, and the intercompany journal?
options: Lesson 19
Lesson 20
Lesson 21
Lesson 23
questions.explain: Lesson 20 investigates Cash Management, Subledger Accounting, and General Ledger — symptoms 4, 5, and 6.

questions.q: At this point in the capstone (end of lesson 18), has any root cause actually been confirmed yet?
options: Yes, all six root causes are already confirmed and corrected
No — the symptoms are named, but tracing them to confirmed root causes is lessons 19 and 20's job
Only the bank variance has been confirmed so far
The lesson states the books were never actually out of balance at all
questions.explain: Lesson 18 only names the symptoms as Elena describes them; confirming root causes is explicitly left to lessons 19 and 20.
